node_definition.done_when: Read section 42 of crew-runtime-positive-controls first. In reckon/crew/dispatch.py, _claim_holder_is_alive treats a pid it cannot interrogate, including one beyond the C int range that makes os.kill raise OverflowError, as a holder still present, so the dispatch refuses under D12 rather than raising. An empty or unreadable claim file whose modification time is older than a short bound is reclaimed as a dead holder's claim is. Choose the bound as a named constant of a few seconds, longer than the record write takes. An empty claim younger than the bound still refuses. tests/test_concurrent_dispatch_of_one_node.py gains three cases: a 10**30 pid refuses without raising, a stale empty claim is reclaimed and the dispatch proceeds, and a fresh empty claim refuses. The first two fail at your base. Existing cases in that file and tests reaching _claim_node_dispatch keep passing; grep tests/ for _claim_node_dispatch, _claim_holder_is_alive and D12 to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/node-claim-survives-a-corrupt-record.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
